descriptionChirho: The aromatic resin mor, a costly spice derived from the Commiphora tree, used in sacred anointing oil (Exod 30:23), burial preparations, and as a perfume in the Song of Songs. All three clusters represent the identical substance with grammatical variation: absolute ('myrrh'), with article ('the-myrrh'), construct ('myrrh-of'), and with 1cs suffix ('my-myrrh'). Uniformly attested: English 'myrrh/the-myrrh', Spanish 'mirra/mi-mirra', Hindi 'gandhras (गंधरस/गन्धरस)', Arabic 'mur (مُور/مُرّاً/الْمُرِّ)', Korean 'molyak (몰약)', Swahili 'manemane'. No semantic differentiation exists; all inflections denote the same aromatic substance.
